chapter: Reel 3: defining jazz and the blues
title: Johnson's poem on the blues
summary: He recites a poem about the blues from the anthology he wrote at 71, and they mention Leadbelly.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the blues is, and why every jazz player needs it

blocks.x: Well, you first have to tell me what is jazz.

Well, that's the question, that's the question. I've got a lot of definitions on jazz, and a definition is really elusive, so when we talk about defining it, we know that it's a feeling, we know it's something you feel; let's see -- I think it was -- I was trying to remember who said, 'If you don't feel it, you will never know what it is.' That could have been any number of people.
Yes, sure. If you don't enjoy it, you can't splice it, you see. 'Take a slice of bad breaks
and a dish of heartaches, and take a heaping cup of letdowns, and mix them well, and pass them off as the blues around.

"Blues mostly get born and then grow up in the wilderness of misfortune, akin to misery of a soul full of sorrow -- a product of America, made of tombstone grief, without a mother and without a father.

"The blues grow fat feeding on hearts, full of unhappiness -- washed down with hot tears of solitude and loneliness. Folks play the blues, they sing the blues, they walk and talk and cry the blues, when they've got the blues by the tail and can't let go.

"The blues marry eternity, or didn't you know? I'm gonna laugh in your face when I see you in your coffin gown, I'll fling some mud on your grave when they lower your frame in the ground, and then I will stand there and cry until the noon day sun goes down.
"The blues can nudge a steel hearted man to his knees. Blues -- just a black folk disease.
What you've just heard is a poem on the blues that J.C. wrote, and included in an anthology of poetry that he put together when he was 71 years old.
Leadbelly said that all blacks are born with the blues, but now everybody has the blues.

Right. But now everybody has them.
Yeah. Well, everybody does have it.
